subsection.title: Target User and Core Problem
subsection.description: - Identify the main target user and the core problem the product should address. - Include the user's situation or current consequence when it helps explain the problem. - Mention the current workaround or evidence only when it materially clarifies the problem. - Do not ask for a solution, screen, technology, requirement list, or demo procedure.
subsection.example: Shoppers who browse without an account lose the products they collected when they sign in to check out, so they rebuild the cart or leave without buying.

subsection.title: Intent and Desired Outcome
subsection.description: - State what the product intends to change for the target user, the final outcome they should gain, and why it matters to the business. - Preserve priorities and scope boundaries the user supplied so later proposals cannot pursue a different purpose. Do not invent exclusions or a separate intent field. - Preserve a measurement signal when the user already has one; Section 6 turns it into a KPI. Do not require a metric or start a metrics interview here. - Do not invent business claims or measures the user did not provide or approve.
subsection.example: Shoppers keep what they collected as guests when they sign in, so the store recovers purchases that are abandoned at sign-in. Keeping members' existing carts intact matters more than speed of rollout.
